title: openEHR Data Structures Information Model
description: OOJS representation of the openEHR RM data_structures package (RM Release 1.1.0). Covers the item_structure, representation, and history packages, together with the LOCATABLE ancestry types from the common RM that are required as bases.

ARCHETYPED.description: Archetype identification metadata attached to archetype root points. Records the archetype_id, optional template_id, and the RM version used to create the object.

rm_version.description: Version of the openEHR RM used to create this object, e.g. '1.1.0'.

LINK.description: A logical relationship between two archetyped structures, expressed as a typed, meaningful directed link to a target DV_EHR_URI.

meaning.description: Clinical description of the relationship, e.g. 'in response to', 'follow-up to'.

type.description: Domain-level type of the link, e.g. 'problem', 'issue'.

target.description: The target object of the link relation.

FEEDER_AUDIT_DETAILS.description: Audit details for one system in a feeder chain: who/where/when the information item was created or handled.

system_id.description: Identifier of the system that handled the item.

version_id.description: Optional version identifier used in the source system.

time.description: Optional time of handling the item.

other_details.description: Optional custom meta-data, may be archetyped.

FEEDER_AUDIT.description: Audit trail describing the origin of data transformed into openEHR form from a feeder or legacy system.

originating_system_item_ids.description: Identifiers for the item in the originating system.

feeder_system_item_ids.description: Identifiers for the item in the feeder system, if distinct from the originating system.

original_content.description: Optional inline or referenced original content.

originating_system_audit.description: Audit information from the originating system.

feeder_system_audit.description: Optional audit information from the feeder system.

LOCATABLE.description: Abstract root of all information model classes that can be archetyped and path-addressed. Carries a runtime name, a design-time archetype_node_id, and optional uid, links, archetype_details, and feeder_audit.

name.description: Runtime name of this node, used to build runtime paths.

archetype_node_id.description: Design-time archetype node identifier, e.g. 'at0005'. At archetype root points this is the stringified archetype_id.

uid.description: Optional globally unique identifier for archetype root points.

links.description: Optional links to other archetyped structures.

archetype_details.description: Archetype identification metadata; present only at archetype root points.

feeder_audit.description: Optional audit trail from a feeder or legacy system.

DATA_STRUCTURE.description: Abstract parent of all data structure types. Each subtype implements as_hierarchy() to produce a CEN EN13606-compatible single-hierarchy representation.

ITEM.description: Abstract parent of the CLUSTER and ELEMENT representation classes. Compatible with ISO 13606-1 classes of the same names.

CLUSTER.description: The grouping variant of ITEM. Contains an ordered list of child ITEM objects (CLUSTERs or ELEMENTs).

items.description: Ordered list of child ITEM objects under this CLUSTER.

ELEMENT.description: The leaf variant of ITEM. Carries a DATA_VALUE and optional null semantics. Exactly one of value or null_flavour must be set.

value.description: The leaf data value. Absent when the element is null.

null_flavour.description: Flavour of null value when value is absent, e.g. 253|unknown|, 271|no information|, 272|masked|, 273|not applicable|.

null_reason.description: Optional specific reason for null value; requires null_flavour to be set.

ITEM_STRUCTURE.description: Abstract parent of all spatial (item-structure) data types: ITEM_SINGLE, ITEM_LIST, ITEM_TABLE, ITEM_TREE.

ITEM_SINGLE.description: Logical single-value data structure. Used for any datum that is logically one value, such as a patient's weight or height.

ITEM_LIST.description: Logical list data structure where each item has a value and can be referred to by name or positional index. Used for blood pressure, protocols, blood tests, etc. Not for time-based lists (use HISTORY instead).

items.description: Physical representation of the list as an ordered sequence of ELEMENTs.

ITEM_TABLE.description: Logical relational-table data structure with named, ordered columns. Implemented as CLUSTER-per-row encoding. Each row CLUSTER contains ELEMENTs with identical names and value types across rows. Used for visual acuity results, reflex test results, etc. Not for time-based data (use HISTORY).

rows.description: Physical representation as an ordered list of row CLUSTERs, each containing one ELEMENT per column.

ITEM_TREE.description: Logical tree data structure. Items may be CLUSTERs (interior nodes) or ELEMENTs (leaf nodes) in any combination. Used for hierarchically structured data such as microbiology or biochemistry results.

items.description: Top-level items of the tree; each may be a CLUSTER or ELEMENT.

EVENT.description: Abstract notion of a single event in a time series. The data attribute holds the event's ITEM_STRUCTURE payload; the optional state attribute holds contextual state data at the time of the event.

time.description: Absolute time of this event. For INTERVAL_EVENT this is the trailing edge of the interval.

data.description: The primary data of this event.

state.description: Optional state data describing the subject's condition at the time of the event, e.g. level of exertion during heart-rate measurement.

POINT_EVENT.description: A single instantaneous event in a time series. The data represents an actual value at a precise point in time.

INTERVAL_EVENT.description: A single interval event in a time series. The data represents a summary value (mean, maximum, change, etc.) over the interval defined by [time - width, time]. The math_function attribute specifies the aggregation applied.

width.description: Duration of the time interval. The event's time attribute is the trailing edge; the leading edge is time - width.

math_function.description: Mathematical function applied to the data over the interval, coded from openEHR vocabulary 'event math function', e.g. 144|maximum|, 146|mean|, 147|change|, 640|actual|.

sample_count.description: Optional count of original fine-grained samples summarised by this interval event.

HISTORY.description: Root object of a linear time series. Contains an ordered list of EVENTs (POINT_EVENT or INTERVAL_EVENT) all sharing the same ITEM_STRUCTURE type for their data. An optional summary attribute holds aggregate or interpretive data for the whole series.

origin.description: Time origin of the series. The first event is not necessarily at the origin; EVENT.offset is computed as EVENT.time - origin.

period.description: Period between samples for a periodic series. Absent for aperiodic series.

duration.description: Optional total duration of the history, covering all events and/or the summary.

events.description: The events in the series, each a POINT_EVENT or INTERVAL_EVENT.

summary.description: Optional summary data that aggregates or interprets the event series, e.g. a radiologist's report or a graphical summary image.
